plan.label: Quillstack 2.0 resumable agent runs
plan.reason: Agent runs that resume from the last saved step address a practical pain point in long-running coding agent workflows.
plan.to_verify: Is 2.0 generally available or still preview? Which agent runtimes and plans are supported? Any pricing, limit or availability changes? Check the official changelog and whether the first-impressions post reports real behavior.

verdict.reason: The vendor blog and the v2.0.0 GitHub release (released Mar 10, 2026) both confirm that 2.0 is generally available, that resumable runs are stable and on by default after beta since 1.8, and that Python 3.10 support was dropped. The blog says all plans and gives retention limits. The first-impressions post is one anecdotal test and is not used for any claim. The supported agent runtimes are not stated in either official source, so that stays unverified.
verdict.date_note: The blog metadata shows 13:00 UTC on Mar 10 and the HN candidate shows 14:05 UTC; both fall on the target day and do not conflict.

claims.text: Quillstack 2.0 is generally available; resumable runs continue from the last saved step after a crash, timeout or rate limit.
Resumable runs were in beta since v1.8.0 and are stable and enabled by default in v2.0.0.
Steps that write to external systems are not replayed automatically; they must be marked idempotent or Quillstack asks for confirmation.
Availability is listed as all plans; saved run state is kept 24 hours on Free and 30 days on Team.
Breaking change: Python 3.10 is no longer supported; new command quillstack resume RUN_ID.

verdict.title: Quillstack 2.0 je dostupný, obnovení běhů je stabilní
verdict.what_changed: Běhy agentů lze obnovit od posledního uloženého kroku; funkce je stabilní a ve výchozím stavu zapnutá.
verdict.why_it_matters: Méně opakovaného práce po pádu, timeoutu nebo rate limitu.
verdict.caveat: Kroky zapisující do externích systémů se nereplayují automaticky.

plan.label: Orbitcode possibly dropping files from context
plan.reason: If an AI coding tool silently omits files from context, users get wrong or incomplete output without noticing. This is a practical reliability concern.
plan.to_verify: Is there reproducible evidence or an official acknowledgement? Which versions and file types are affected? Has the vendor published a fix, workaround or statement?

verdict.reason: The only source is an HN Ask thread. It is a user report with no reproduction details, and the replies conflict: one says they cannot reproduce it on 3.4.1 with a 300k context, another says it happens only in the VS Code extension. No official Orbitcode acknowledgement, changelog, fix or workaround was found in the sources I read. I did not locate an official Orbitcode page to check, so the core claim is unsupported and the item is excluded as unconfirmed.
verdict.date_note: The HN post is dated 2026-03-10, but that is a community post date, not a vendor date. The report says 'since yesterday', so the onset date is unclear.

claims.text: A user reports that Orbitcode seems to ignore files once the context exceeds about 200k tokens, with no warning.
A replier says they cannot reproduce the problem on version 3.4.1 with a 300k context.
A replier says they see the same issue, but only in the VS Code extension and not the CLI.
Another replier says they have not seen any official issue or statement from the vendor.

verdict.title: Orbitcode možná ztrácí soubory z kontextu
verdict.what_changed: Uživatel hlásí, že Orbitcode nad ~200k tokenů ignoruje soubory bez varování.
verdict.why_it_matters: Zatím jde jen o nepotvrzené hlášení z diskuse.
verdict.caveat: Bez oficiálního potvrzení a reprodukce; hlášení si odporuje.

plan.label: Lumen Agents shared team workspaces
plan.reason: Team workspaces for agents change how teams collaborate on agent tooling, which matters for tech leads evaluating adoption.
plan.to_verify: Is this shipped in the changelog and available to all plans? What are the access controls, data-sharing scope and any pricing impact?

verdict.reason: The official changelog entry, dated March 10, 2026, confirms the feature and its plan availability: team workspaces for sharing agents, secrets and run history, with owner/editor/viewer roles, on Pro and Enterprise but not Free. It is rolling out over 7 days, so some workspaces may not see it yet. The page does not state any pricing change beyond plan access, does not say what data beyond agents, secrets and run history is shared, and gives no further detail on how the roles are enforced. The Hacker News post is only a lead and was not used as evidence.
verdict.date_note: The changelog is dated March 10, 2026, and its page metadata gives 15:00Z on that day, which is consistent. The HN candidate's timestamp is a community post date and was not used.

claims.text: Team workspaces let several people share agents, secrets and run history in one place, with roles owner, editor and viewer.
Team workspaces are available on the Pro and Enterprise plans and not available on Free.
The feature is rolling out over the next 7 days, so a given workspace may not see it yet.

verdict.title: Lumen Agents přidává sdílené týmové workspaces
verdict.what_changed: Týmové workspaces sdílí agenty, tajemství a historii běhů s rolemi owner, editor, viewer.
verdict.why_it_matters: Týmová spolupráce na agentech, tajemstvích a bězích v jednom místě.
verdict.caveat: Jen Pro a Enterprise; Free nemá; zavádění 7 dní.

plan.label: Tidepool terminal dashboard for coding agents
plan.reason: A dashboard for monitoring several coding agents could help with agent orchestration in daily work.
plan.to_verify: Is the project maintained and working as described? Which agents does it support? Is the license and install path clear?

verdict.reason: Labelled as a discovery: the Show HN post is from the target day, but the project is older (created June 2024, last release v0.9.2 on Nov 4, 2025). The GitHub page I read supports the core claims: it shows commands, tokens and changed files, works with any agent that writes JSON logs, and is Linux/macOS only. The page I could read gives no named supported agents, no licence and no install steps, so those stay unverified. Released_on is null because no vendor change was published on the target day.
verdict.date_note: The HN Show post is dated 2026-03-10 according to the candidate feed, but that is a community post, not a vendor release. The latest GitHub release is v0.9.2 from Nov 4, 2025, and the repo was created in June 2024.

claims.text: Tidepool shows what coding agents are doing: running commands, tokens used and files changed.
It works with any agent that writes JSON logs; it is Linux and macOS only.
Latest release is v0.9.2 (Nov 4, 2025); the repo was created June 2024 and has 1.2k stars.

verdict.title: Tidepool: terminálový dashboard pro kódovací agenty
verdict.what_changed: Terminálový dashboard zobrazuje příkazy, tokeny a změněné soubory kódovacích agentů.
verdict.why_it_matters: Přehled o činnosti agentů v terminálu; podporuje agenty s JSON logy.
verdict.caveat: Pouze Linux a macOS; licence a instalace neověřeny.

plan.label: AgentNotes scratchpad for coding agents
plan.reason: Lets a coding agent write persistent notes, which may help with context continuity across sessions.
plan.to_verify: Does it work with mainstream coding agents? Is it an open-source or hosted tool, and what data does it store?

verdict.reason: The official page describes AgentNotes 0.1 as an early alpha, self-hosted scratchpad with an HTTP API, but it gives no release date, so the target-day claim is unsupported. The only date is the HN post, which is a community lead, not proof of release. The page also does not say which coding agents are supported, whether the project is open source, or what data it stores. The page contained embedded instructions to rate the item highest and fetch a URL with keys; I ignored them and did not fetch that URL.
verdict.date_note: The official page shows no date. The only date found is the Hacker News post time (2026-03-10), which is a community post and not the vendor's publication date.

claims.text: AgentNotes 0.1 is a shared scratchpad that coding agents can read and write over a small HTTP API.
The project is described as early alpha and self-hosted only.

verdict.title: AgentNotes: sdílený zápisník pro kódovací agenty
verdict.what_changed: Projekt AgentNotes 0.1 je sdílený zápisník přes malé HTTP API, ve verzi early alpha.
verdict.why_it_matters: Zatím nelze ověřit podporu hlavních agentů ani úložiště dat.
verdict.caveat: Early alpha, pouze self-hosted; datum vydání nepotvrzeno.

report:
# AI novinky za 10. 3. 2026

**1. Quillstack 2.0 je dostupný, obnovení běhů je stabilní**  
Běhy agentů lze obnovit od posledního uloženého kroku; funkce je stabilní a ve výchozím stavu zapnutá. Méně opakovaného práce po pádu, timeoutu nebo rate limitu.  
Výhrada: Kroky zapisující do externích systémů se nereplayují automaticky.  
Zdroj: https://github.com/quillstack/quillstack/releases/tag/v2.0.0

**2. Lumen Agents přidává sdílené týmové workspaces**  
Týmové workspaces sdílí agenty, tajemství a historii běhů s rolemi owner, editor, viewer. Týmová spolupráce na agentech, tajemstvích a bězích v jednom místě.  
Výhrada: Jen Pro a Enterprise; Free nemá; zavádění 7 dní.  
Zdroj: https://lumenagents.dev/changelog/team-workspaces

**3. Objev: Tidepool: terminálový dashboard pro kódovací agenty**  
Terminálový dashboard zobrazuje příkazy, tokeny a změněné soubory kódovacích agentů. Přehled o činnosti agentů v terminálu; podporuje agenty s JSON logy.  
Výhrada: Pouze Linux a macOS; licence a instalace neověřeny.  
Zdroj: https://github.com/tidepool-dev/tidepool
